rationale: Both independently surface the same high-value uncaught finding (identical NPU-runner twin bug), the async_chunk default-fallback inconsistency, and the AMD CI failure, giving them comparable recall/precision over the largely-already-resolved ground-truth items. Y edges ahead on actionability with ready-to-apply suggestion diffs and explicit tool-verified evidence (gh_ci_read, grep confirmations), and its proposed mixed-per-request-token-count test case is the closer match to the latent multi-axis batch-splitting gap that X's padding-focused hardening note doesn't quite reach. X's review is deeper in places (streaming consumer-disagreement analysis, WS realtime path) but slightly more speculative in its root-cause claims.
